children.translated_text: I salute the most blissful <s>Guru</s>,
whose form is the embodiment of one's own bliss,
by whose mere proximity
the body becomes filled with the bliss of consciousness.
Through <s>ādhāra</s> (root support), <s>bandha</s> (lock), and other practices, with the inner lamp-bud of the motionless self,
that <s>yogī</s> who is celebrated through the reckoning of an age-long <s>kalpa</s> period,
from whom arose the great ocean of the fragrance of knowledge, where <s>Ādinātha</s> himself manifested,
I worship unceasingly <s>Śrī Mīnanātha</s>, who transcends the qualities of the manifest and unmanifest.
Having saluted the <s>Guru</s> with devotion,
<s>Gorakṣa</s> speaks the supreme knowledge
desired by <s>yogīs</s>,
which bestows the highest bliss.
<s>Gorakṣa</s> speaks the <s>Śataka</s> (hundred verses)
desiring the welfare of <s>yogīs</s>;
by the understanding of which, certainly,
the supreme state is attained.
This is the stairway to liberation,
this is the deception of death;
by which the mind, turned away from delusion,
becomes attached to the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self).
The fruit of the wish-fulfilling tree of the <s>Śruti</s> (scriptures), whose branches are frequented by the twice-born,
the fruit of the wish-fulfilling tree of the <s>Śruti</s>,
the remedy for the afflictions of worldly existence —
the virtuous person embraces <s>Yoga</s>.
<s>Āsana</s> (posture), <s>prāṇa-saṃyāma</s> (breath control),
<s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of senses), and <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration),
<s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) — these
are the six limbs of <s>Yoga</s>.
The <s>āsanas</s> (postures) are as many
as there are species of living beings.
All the varieties of these
<s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord) alone knows.
Out of eighty-four <s>lakṣas</s> (8,400,000),
one from each has been described.
From those, by <s>Śiva</s>,
eighty-four seats have been designated as the best sixteen hundred.
Of all the <s>āsanas</s>,
two alone are distinguished as excellent:
one is called <s>Siddhāsana</s> (the adept's posture),
the second is <s>Kamalāsana</s> (the lotus posture).
Placing the heel firmly at the <s>yoni-sthāna</s> (perineum),

children.text: meḍhre pādam athaikam eva niyataṃ kṛtvā samaṃ vigraham
children.translated_text: one should place the other foot firmly upon the <s>meḍhra</s> (generative organ), keeping the body straight;
like a pillar, with senses restrained, gazing steadily at the space between the eyebrows,
this is called <s>Siddhāsana</s>, which produces the breaking open of the door to liberation.

children.text: vāmorūpari dakṣiṇaṃ hi caraṇaṃ saṃsthāpya vāmaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Placing the right foot on the left thigh, and likewise the left

children.text: dakṣorūpari paścimena vidhinā dhṛtvā karābhyāṃ dṛḍham
children.translated_text: on the right thigh, holding firmly with both hands from behind,

children.text: aṅguṣṭhau hṛdaye nidhāya cibukaṃ nāsāgram ālokayed
children.translated_text: placing the thumbs on the chest and the chin, one should gaze at the tip of the nose —
this is called <s>Padmāsana</s> (lotus posture) of the <s>yamīs</s> (self-controlled ones), which removes diseases and ailments.
The six <s>cakras</s> (energy centers), the sixteen supports,
the three <s>lakṣyas</s> (targets of meditation), the five <s>vyomas</s> (spaces) —
those who do not know these in their own body,
how can such <s>yogīs</s> attain perfection?
The body is a house with one pillar and nine doors,
presided over by five deities —
those who do not know their own body,
how can such <s>yogīs</s> attain perfection?
The <s>Ādhāra</s> (root center) has four petals,
<s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s> has six petals,
at the navel is a lotus of ten petals,
at the heart is one with the number of petals equal to the sun (twelve).
At the throat there are sixteen petals,
between the eyebrows, two petals;
the thousand-petaled lotus is proclaimed
at the <s>Brahma-randhra</s> (aperture of Brahman), the great pathway.
<s>Ādhāra</s> is the first <s>cakra</s>,
<s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s> is the second;
the <s>yoni-sthāna</s> (seat of origin) between the two
is called <s>Kāma-rūpa</s> (the form of desire).
The place called <s>Ādhāra</s>, situated at the anus,
is a lotus of four petals;
in its center is proclaimed the <s>yoni</s> (source),
called <s>Kāmākṣā</s>, venerated by the <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected beings).
In the middle of the <s>yoni</s> stands the great <s>liṅga</s>,
facing westward;
one who knows the jewel-like disc at its head
is a knower of <s>Yoga</s>.
Shining like molten gold,
flashing like a streak of lightning,
triangular is that citadel of fire,
established below the <s>meḍhra</s> (generative organ).
That supreme light seen in <s>samādhi</s> (absorption),
infinite and facing in all directions —
when that is seen in the great <s>Yoga</s>,
there is no more coming and going (cycle of rebirth).
By the word 'sva' is meant <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath);
<s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s> is its abode.
Because of the word <s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s>,
the <s>meḍhra</s> (generative organ) itself is so designated.
Where the <s>kanda</s> (bulb) is threaded by the <s>Suṣumṇā</s> like a jewel on a thread,
where the <s>kanda</s> is strung upon the <s>Suṣumṇā</s>,
that region of the navel <s>cakra</s>
is called <s>Maṇipūraka</s> (the jewel-filled center).
In the great <s>cakra</s> of twelve spokes (petals),
free from merit and demerit,
the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) wanders
as long as it does not discover the truth.
Above the <s>meḍhra</s> and below the navel,
the <s>kanda-yoni</s> (root-bulb) is like a bird's egg;
from there the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) arise,
seventy-two thousand in number.
Among those thousands of <s>nāḍīs</s>,
seventy-two are described as notable;
the principal ones that carry <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath) —
of those, ten are further remembered as chief.
<s>Iḍā</s> and <s>Piṅgalā</s>,
and <s>Suṣumṇā</s> as the third,
<s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Hasti-jihvā</s>,
<s>Pūṣā</s>, and <s>Yaśasvinī</s>,
<s>Alambuṣā</s>, <s>Kuhū</s>,
and <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> is remembered as the tenth.
This <s>cakra</s> composed of <s>nāḍīs</s>
should always be known by <s>yogīs</s>.
<s>Iḍā</s> is situated on the left side,
<s>Piṅgalā</s> on the right likewise;
<s>Suṣumṇā</s> is in the central region,
<s>Gāndhārī</s> is in the left eye.
<s>Hasti-jihvā</s> is in the right eye,
<s>Pūṣā</s> is in the right ear,
<s>Yaśasvinī</s> is in the left ear,
and <s>Alambuṣā</s> is in the mouth.
<s>Kuhū</s> is in the region of the generative organ,
and <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> is at the <s>mūla-sthāna</s> (root place).
Thus, situated at the doors (of the body),
the ten <s>nāḍīs</s> abide.
<s>Iḍā</s>, <s>Piṅgalā</s>, and <s>Suṣumṇā</s> —
these three <s>nāḍīs</s> are described as principal.
They constantly carry <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath),
having <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and <s>Agni</s> as their presiding deities.
<s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Samāna</s>,
<s>Udāna</s>, and <s>Vyāna</s> are the five <s>vāyus</s> (vital airs);
<s>Nāga</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, <s>Kṛkara</s>,
<s>Devadatta</s>, and <s>Dhanañjaya</s>.
<s>Prāṇa</s> always dwells in the heart,
<s>Apāna</s> in the region of the anus,
<s>Samāna</s> is in the region of the navel,
<s>Udāna</s> moves in the middle of the throat.
<s>Nāga</s> is known for belching,
<s>Kūrma</s> is remembered for the opening of the eyes,
<s>Kṛkara</s> should be known as causing sneezing,
<s>Devadatta</s> is for yawning.
<s>Dhanañjaya</s>, which is all-pervading, does not leave
even the dead body.
All these, in the form of the <s>jīva</s> (life force),
move through all the <s>nāḍīs</s>.
Just as a ball, when struck with a stick,
bounces upward,
so the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), tossed by <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s>,
does not remain still.
The <s>jīva</s>, under the control of <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s>,
runs downward and upward;
through the left and right pathways,
due to its restlessness, it cannot be seen.
Just as a hawk, bound by a rope,
even when it flies away, is pulled back,
so the <s>jīva</s>, bound by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature),
is pulled by <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s>.
<s>Apāna</s> pulls <s>Prāṇa</s>,
and <s>Prāṇa</s> pulls <s>Apāna</s>;
these two, situated above and below,
the knower of <s>Yoga</s> unites them.
With the syllable 'ha' the breath goes out,
with the syllable 'sa' it enters again;
'<s>Haṃsa</s>, <s>Haṃsa</s>' — this <s>mantra</s>
the <s>jīva</s> recites constantly.
Six hundred times in a day and night,
twenty-one thousand six hundred times —
this <s>mantra</s>, endowed with this number,
the <s>jīva</s> recites constantly.
This is called the <s>Ajapā Gāyatrī</s> (unrepeated prayer),
which bestows liberation upon <s>yogīs</s>.
By the mere intention of this,
one is freed from all sins.
There is no knowledge equal to this,
there is no <s>japa</s> (recitation) equal to this,
there is no wisdom equal to this —
there never was, nor ever shall be.
Born from <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>,
this <s>Gāyatrī</s> sustains the <s>Prāṇa</s> (life breath).
The knowledge of <s>Prāṇa</s> is the great knowledge;
one who knows this is a knower of <s>Yoga</s>.
Above the <s>kanda</s> (bulb), the <s>Kuṇḍalinī Śakti</s>
is coiled eightfold in the shape of a coil.
She always covers the mouth
of the <s>Brahma-dvāra</s> (door of Brahman) with her mouth.
Through which door one must travel
to reach the painless abode of <s>Brahman</s> —
covering that door with her mouth,
the supreme goddess lies asleep.
Awakened by the union with fire,
and by the mind and the wind (<s>vāyu</s>),
she rises upward through the <s>Suṣumṇā</s>
like a needle drawing a thread.
In the form of a quivering serpent,
beautiful like a lotus fiber,
awakened by the union with fire,
she travels upward through the <s>Suṣumṇā</s>.
Just as one opens a door
forcefully with a key,
so the <s>yogī</s> should break open the door of liberation
with <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> by force (<s>haṭha</s>).

children.text: kṛtvā sampuṭitau karau dṛḍhataraṃ baddhvā tu padmāsanaṃ
children.translated_text: Making a cup with both hands, sitting firmly in <s>Padmāsana</s> (lotus posture),

children.text: gāḍhaṃ vakṣasi sannidhāya cibukaṃ dhyātvā ca tat prekṣitam
children.translated_text: pressing the chin firmly against the chest, meditating and gazing upon that,

children.text: vāraṃ vāram apānam ūrdhvam anilaṃ proccārayet pūritaṃ
children.translated_text: again and again raising the <s>Apāna</s> breath upward and releasing the filled air,

children.text: muñcan prāṇam upaiti bodham atulaṃ śakti-prabodhān naraḥ
children.translated_text: releasing the <s>Prāṇa</s>, a person attains incomparable awakening through the arousal of <s>Śakti</s>.
One should rub the limbs
with the perspiration produced from exertion.
Avoiding pungent, sour, and salty foods,
one should follow a diet of milk.
One who is a <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate), moderate in diet,
renounced, and devoted to <s>Yoga</s>,
becomes a <s>Siddha</s> (perfected one) within a year —
there should be no doubt about this.
Food that is well-oiled and sweet,
leaving one-fourth of the stomach empty,
eaten for the pleasure of the gods —
this is called <s>mitāhāra</s> (moderate diet).
Above the <s>kanda</s> (bulb), the <s>Kuṇḍalinī Śakti</s>
is coiled eightfold in the shape of a coil.
For the deluded, she is the cause of bondage;
for <s>yogīs</s>, she is remembered as the bestower of liberation.
One who knows <s>Mahāmudrā</s> (the great seal), <s>Namo-mudrā</s> (the bowing seal),
<s>Uḍḍiyāna</s> (the upward flying lock), <s>Jālandhara</s> (the throat lock),
and <s>Mūla-bandha</s> (the root lock) —
that <s>yogī</s> is a vessel of <s>siddhis</s> (perfections).
The purification of the network of <s>nāḍīs</s>,
the movement of the moon and sun (channels),
and the drying up of the bodily fluids —
this is called <s>Mahāmudrā</s> (the great seal).

children.text: vakṣo-nyasta-hanur nipīḍya suciraṃ yoniṃ ca vāmāṅghriṇā
children.translated_text: Pressing the chin against the chest, pressing the <s>yoni</s> (perineum) firmly with the left heel,

children.text: hastābhyām avadhāritaṃ prasaritaṃ pādaṃ tathā dakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: holding the extended right foot with both hands,

children.text: āpūrya śvasanena kukṣi-yugalaṃ baddhvā śanai recayed
children.translated_text: filling both sides of the belly with breath and then slowly releasing —

children.text: eṣā pātaka-nāśinī sumahatī mudrā nṝṇāṃ procyate
children.translated_text: this is called the great <s>Mudrā</s> for people, which destroys all sins.
Having practiced first on the left side (moon),
one should then practice on the right side (sun);
when the count becomes equal on both sides,
then one should release the <s>mudrā</s>.
Neither wholesome nor unwholesome food
all flavors become tasteless,
even deadly poison once consumed
is digested like nectar.
Consumption, leprosy, intestinal disorders,
abdominal tumors, indigestion, and other such ailments—
all these afflictions are destroyed
for one who practices <s>Mahāmudrā</s> (the great seal).
This <s>Mahāmudrā</s> has been described
as bestowing great <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers) upon people.
It should be kept secret with great effort
and not given to just anyone.
The tongue enters into
the cavity of the skull, turned upward;
the gaze is directed between the eyebrows—
this <s>mudrā</s> is known as <s>Khecarī</s> (moving through space).
Neither disease nor death nor drowsiness,
neither sleep nor hunger nor thirst,
nor fainting afflicts the one
who knows <s>Khecarī Mudrā</s>.
One is not afflicted by disease,
nor tainted by <s>karma</s> (action),
nor overpowered by time (death)—
one who knows <s>Khecarī Mudrā</s>.
The mind moves in space (<s>kha</s>), and
the tongue also moves, having entered space—
therefore this is named <s>Khecarī</s>,
a <s>mudrā</s> defined by the <s>siddhas</s> (perfected ones).
<s>Bindu</s> (the vital essence) is the root of the body,
and the <s>śirās</s> (veins/channels) are established therein;
they sustain the body
from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head.
By one who has sealed with <s>Khecarī</s>
the opening above the <s>lambikā</s> (uvula),
<s>bindu</s> does not flow downward,
even when embraced by a woman.
As long as <s>bindu</s> remains in the body,
how can there be fear of death?
As long as <s>Nabho Mudrā</s> (the space seal) is held,
<s>bindu</s> does not depart.
Even when <s>bindu</s> has moved
and reached the fire (<s>hutāśana</s>),
it is drawn upward by <s>Śakti</s> (spiritual energy)
and restrained by <s>Yoni Mudrā</s> (the womb seal).
That <s>bindu</s> is of two kinds:
white and red.
The white is called <s>śukra</s> (semen),
and the red is called <s>mahārajas</s> (the great rajas).
Resembling liquid vermillion,
<s>rajas</s> resides in the seat of the sun;
<s>bindu</s> resides in the seat of the moon—
the union of these two is extremely difficult to attain.
<s>Bindu</s> is <s>Śiva</s>, <s>rajas</s> is <s>Śakti</s>;
<s>bindu</s> is the moon, <s>rajas</s> is the sun.
Only through the union of both
is the supreme state attained.
When <s>mahārajas</s>, impelled
by the movement of <s>Śakti</s> through the wind (<s>vāyu</s>),
merges into oneness with <s>bindu</s>,
then the body becomes divine.
<s>Śukra</s> (semen) is united with the moon,
<s>rajas</s> is united with the sun;
one who brings about the harmonious unity of these two
is a true knower of <s>yoga</s>.
Because the great bird (<s>mahā-khaga</s>, i.e., <s>prāṇa</s>) flies upward
without rest through it,
it is called <s>Uḍḍīyāna</s> (flying up)—
this <s>bandha</s> (lock) is thus described.
Behind the abdomen,
below the navel, it is said—
this is <s>Uḍḍīyāna Bandha</s> (the flying-up lock);
there the lock is applied.
It binds the network of channels (<s>sirā-jāla</s>)
through which the cranial fluid flows downward;
hence it is called <s>Jālandhara Bandha</s> (the net-holding lock),
the destroyer of the mass of afflictions in the throat.
When <s>Jālandhara Bandha</s> is performed,
characterized by the contraction of the throat,
the nectar (<s>pīyūṣa</s>) does not fall into the [digestive] fire,
and the breath (<s>vāyu</s>) is not disturbed.
Pressing the perineum with the heel,
one should contract the anus and draw up the <s>yoni</s> (perineum);
drawing <s>Apāna</s> (the downward breath) upward—
this is called <s>Mūla Bandha</s> (the root lock).
Through the union of <s>Apāna</s> and <s>Prāṇa</s>,
and the diminishing of urine and feces,
even an old person becomes youthful
by constant practice of <s>Mūla Bandha</s>.
Having assumed <s>Padmāsana</s> (the lotus posture),
with body and head held erect,
gazing at the tip of the nose, in solitude,
one should repeat the imperishable <s>Oṃkāra</s>.
<s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>—these are the three worlds;
<s>Soma</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and <s>Agni</s> are the deities;
in whose <s>mātrās</s> (measures) they abide—
that is the supreme light, <s>Oṃ</s>.
The three times, the three <s>Vedas</s>,
the three worlds, the three musical notes,
the three gods abide in which—
that is the supreme light, <s>Oṃ</s>.
<s>Kriyā</s> (action), <s>Icchā</s> (will), and <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge);
<s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Raudrī</s>, and <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>—
the threefold <s>Śakti</s> abides in which—
that is the supreme light, <s>Oṃ</s>.
The syllable <s>a</s>, then the syllable <s>u</s>,
and the syllable <s>m</s>, known as <s>bindu</s>—
the three <s>mātrās</s> abide in which—
that is the supreme light, <s>Oṃ</s>.
One should recite that seed (<s>bīja</s>) with speech,
practice it with the body,
and remember it always with the mind—
that is the supreme light, <s>Oṃ</s>.
Whether pure or impure,
one who constantly recites <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>)
is not tainted by sin,
just as a lotus leaf is not [wetted] by water.
When the breath (<s>vāyu</s>) is unsteady, <s>bindu</s> is unsteady;
when it is still, [<s>bindu</s>] becomes still.
The <s>yogī</s> attains steadfastness—
therefore one should restrain the breath.
As long as the breath remains in the body,
that is called life;
death is its departure—
therefore one should restrain the breath.
As long as the breath is held in the body,
as long as the mind is free from agitation,
as long as the gaze is between the eyebrows—
how can there be fear of death?
Therefore, out of fear of death, <s>Brahmā</s> [himself]
is devoted to <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control),
as are <s>yogīs</s> and sages—
therefore one should restrain the breath.
The <s>haṃsa</s> (breath) measuring thirty-six finger-breadths
travels outward
through the left and right pathways—
therefore it is called <s>prāṇa</s> (the life-breath).
When the entire network of <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels),
filled with impurities, becomes purified,
only then does the <s>yogī</s> become
capable of controlling <s>prāṇa</s>.
Seated in <s>Baddha Padmāsana</s> (the bound lotus posture), the <s>yogī</s>
should inhale <s>prāṇa</s> through the moon (<s>Iḍā</s>, the left nostril),
retain it as long as able,
and then exhale through the sun (<s>Piṅgalā</s>, the right nostril).
Meditating on the disc of the moon
as nectar resembling curd,
like cow's milk or silver—
the practitioner of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> becomes blissful.
Drawing the breath through the right [nostril],
one should fill the abdomen slowly;
having retained it according to the prescribed method,
one should exhale through the moon (the left nostril).
Meditating on the solar disc
as a mass of blazing, flaming fire
situated at the navel, the <s>yogī</s>
becomes blissful through <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.

children.text: prāṇaṃ codiḍayā piben parimitaṃ bhūyo'nyayā recayet
children.translated_text: One should inhale <s>prāṇa</s> through <s>Iḍā</s> (the left channel) in measured amount, then exhale through the other;

children.text: pītvā piṅgalayā samīraṇam atho baddhvā tyajed vāmayā
children.translated_text: having inhaled air through <s>Piṅgalā</s> (the right channel), one should retain it and then release through the left.
For one who meditates on the two discs of the sun and moon through this method,

children.text: śuddhā nāḍi-gaṇā bhavanti yamino māsa-trayād ūrdhvataḥ
children.translated_text: the entire network of <s>nāḍīs</s> becomes purified after three months, O practitioner of restraint (<s>yamin</s>).
Retention of breath at will,
the kindling of the [digestive] fire,
the manifestation of the inner sound (<s>nāda</s>), and good health—
